title: Activation waves & operator playbook for Private/VPC features (RBAC, Audit, KMS)
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: Define a staged activation approach and an operator playbook for the Private/VPC on-prem feature set (RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration). Goal is to minimize risky migrations, give customers clear operator steps, and align cross-functional teams on release notes, training, and telemetry.

Scope: Ship activation procedures and communication assets for: RBAC role mapping and default policies; audit log configuration and retention; KMS key provisioning, rotation guidance, and HSM/KMS integration notes; operator CLI commands and Console onboarding flows; migration checklist for existing Hosted customers moving to Dedicated/Private.

Out-of-scope: New runtime kernel work, major infra refactors, paid private pricing changes. Those are tracked in separate ENG tickets.

Rollout approach: Three activation waves to reduce blast radius and collect operator feedback: 1) Internal activation (Redwood ops + SRE partners) to validate telemetry, alerts, and CLI workflows. 2) Beta cohort of 6 customers (managed enablement with Solutions Engineers) for real-world migrations and runbooks. 3) Opt-in public activation with automated console flows and a documented rollback path. Each wave includes a 72-hour validation window and a defined rollback trigger set.

Cross-team GTM tasks: Coordinate with Docs (detailed migration runbook + FAQ), Developer Experience (console banners & in-UI tips), Sales (beta playbook & positioning deck), Support (TTR playbook + sample logs), Legal & Compliance (customer-facing security statement), and Marketing (release notes summary and targeted comms for enterprise accounts).

Release notes coordination: Draft three pieces — a short public release note, a detailed upgrade guide for admins, and an internal ops bulletin with known limitations and troubleshooting. Highlight KMS caveats (customer-managed keys vs. Redwood-managed fallback) and RBAC default-deny behavior. Include link placeholders to confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/private-activation-playbook and to PRs and GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-operator/pulls.

Acceptance criteria and success metrics: See acceptance_criteria field below. KPIs to monitor post-activation: number of successful private activations, mean time to first successful API call post-migration, rollback rate, and number of enablement escalations.

Risks & mitigations: Key risks are misconfigured KMS keys causing unavailability, RBAC mis-mapping leading to privilege gaps, and missing audit records. Mitigations include preflight checks in the operator CLI, a dry-run audit mode, and mandatory smoke tests before wave progression.

Artifacts: Links to design spec, operator CLI RFC, and training slides will be attached in doc PRs and the confluence page above.
acceptance_criteria: Operator CLI includes 'preflight' command that validates RBAC, KMS access, and audit destination (tests run locally and against a staging control plane)
Console shows step-by-step activation flow and exposes a one-click dry-run for audit config
KMS integration docs include key creation, rotation policy, and recovery steps; legal has reviewed customer-managed key language
Beta cohort (>=6 customers) completes migration with fewer than 2 high-severity support escalations
Telemetry dashboards capture activation events, KMS errors, RBAC rejections, and audit write failures
Release notes published in three formats: public summary, admin upgrade guide, internal ops bulletin
